summary: Env-gated OpenTelemetry OTLP/HTTP metrics exporter harness for the shared hyperscaler metrics port.
claim_boundary: This slice adds a separate OTLP/HTTP adapter crate that implements the existing HyperscalerMetrics trait with OpenTelemetry SDK counters/gauges and an OTLP MetricExporter configured only when OYA_BACKBONE_OTLP_METRICS is enabled and an OTLP endpoint is provided. Default local/CI runs do not contact a collector. It does not claim a live collector deployment, live OTLP export, Alertmanager/Prometheus alert firing, production SLO burn evidence, or production backpressure/circuit-breaker drill.

source_basis.use: Official opentelemetry-otlp 0.32.0 docs for MetricExporter::builder, HTTP/protobuf transport, endpoint/timeout configuration, and SdkMeterProvider::with_periodic_exporter.
Official OpenTelemetry Rust metrics API docs for Meter counter/gauge construction and Counter::add / Gauge::record usage.
Official OpenTelemetry metrics API specification for counter and gauge instrument semantics.

facets.F1_simplicity: The OTLP integration is a separate adapter crate and reuses the existing HyperscalerMetrics port, avoiding OpenTelemetry dependencies in kernel/domain/usecase crates.
facets.F2_hyperscaler: Backbone services now have a compile-checked OTLP/HTTP exporter path that can point at cloud or self-hosted collectors later, with explicit environment gating and honest non-claims for live deployment.
facets.F3_adversarial: Tests cover disabled export, enabled-without-endpoint failure, endpoint precedence, TLS-required rejection for http endpoints, invalid booleans, invalid timeout windows, disabled builder behavior, and runtime outcome recording without a collector.
facets.F4_api_contract: No existing metrics kernel trait changes were required; the new public API is config/error/summary types plus build_otlp_hyperscaler_metrics for composition roots.
facets.F5_quality: Focused OTLP adapter tests plus the 47-package backbone check/test/clippy/fmt matrix, cargo-deny, license-policy, cargo-prefix, catalog/data-class known-blocker probes, parse/config validation, dependency-seam, honest-claims, and diff hygiene are part of this run.
facets.F6_operations: Operators must set OYA_BACKBONE_OTLP_METRICS and a metrics-specific or generic OTLP endpoint; OYA_BACKBONE_OTLP_REQUIRE_TLS enforces https endpoints, and OYA_BACKBONE_OTLP_TIMEOUT_MS bounds exporter timeout.
facets.F7_security_privacy: The adapter emits low-cardinality INTERNAL_ONLY labels only: microservice, capability_id, state, and tenant_id for 429 counters. It never stores credentials or request bodies in code/evidence.
facets.F8_supply_chain: New third-party dependencies are isolated to oya-shared-hyperscaler-metrics-adapter-otlp and documented in dependency rationales for opentelemetry, opentelemetry-otlp, and opentelemetry_sdk.
facets.F9_testing: Focused OTLP adapter tests passed for 6 unit tests. The broad backbone matrix passed 304 unit tests across 47 packages plus one existing ignored metrics adapter doctest.
facets.F10_ci_cd: GitHub Actions and all four Jenkins package matrices include the OTLP adapter package; static workflow/catalog parsing is covered locally, but no remote CI run is claimed.
facets.F11_observability: The adapter maps canonical request/capability metric families to OpenTelemetry synchronous counters and gauges and configures an OTLP MetricExporter with HTTP/protobuf transport when enabled.
facets.F13_reversibility: The change is isolated to one adapter crate, matrix/catalog/rationale entries, and task/evidence metadata; removing the crate and matrix entries reverts the integration without touching service business logic.
